page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 2 physical cores with hyper-threading, resulting in 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core profile but limited multi-core scaling. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core performance is comparatively weak, as seen in the stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Passmark CPU score. Memory bandwidth is also on the lower end, with uncached read speeds at 32.39 GB/sec and write speeds at 20.69 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model reach an average of 145.07 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-4 offers high memory density per vCPU, making it a viable option for workloads requiring substantial RAM without the cost of excess compute cores. However, the tradeoff is its lower multi-core and memory bandwidth efficiency under heavy parallel loads. This instance is best suited for memory-bound, single-threaded or lightly threaded applications, such as text processing, basic web serving, small-scale database operations, and lightweight LLM inference tasks that benefit from dedicated Intel Xeon execution units and AMX instructions.
